Macrons

Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

future noun and adjective

also the future, in future, in the future, from now on

classical

Caes. BC 1.52: nōn sōlum inopiā praesentis, sed etiam futūrī temporis (Lewis & Short)
Hor. C. 3.29.29: prūdēns futūrī temporis exitum (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 87, 319

tempus futūrum, temporis futūrī n.

noun, third declension, with an adjective

the future, time to come

Other words

  • posthāc — in future, from now on

    adverb · also used · classical · Plaut. Men. 4.3.21: aliam posthāc invenītō (Lewis & Short); Catull. 99.16: numquam posthāc (Lewis & Short); Traupman 319

  • in posterum — for the future

    phrase · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 2.8.1: longē in posterum prōspicere (Lewis & Short); Traupman 87, 319

  • futūrus, futūra, futūrum — future, to come

    adjective: future participle of sum · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 70: frūctūs futūrōs; Liv. 1.8.4: futūrae multitūdinis

Examples

  • tempora autem reī pūblicae quālia futūra sint quis scit? mihi quidem turbulenta videntur fore

    but who knows what the political future holds? To me it looks stormyCic. Fam. 2.18.3

  • dum loquimur, fūgerit invida aetās: carpe diem, quam minimum crēdula posterō

    while we talk, envious time will have fled: seize the day, and trust as little as you can to the futureHor. C. 1.11.7–8

See also tomorrow, later, history, period.

SourcesLewis & Short: tempus · Lewis & Short: futurus · Lewis & Short: posthac · Lewis & Short: posterus
